newsitem.title: USA: Dollar nearly at four-month low vs yen as rumors swirl.
newsitem.headline: Dollar nearly at four-month low vs yen as rumors swirl.

text.p: NEW YORK, May 14 - The dollar tumbled on Wednesday to its lowest level against the yen in nearly four months as foreign exchange markets were roiled by rumours that the U.S. Treasury would support a stronger Japanese currency.
Specifically, market gossip claimed that a newsletter from a Washington-based consulting firm stated that U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin is calling for an exchange rate of 115 yen per dollar.
Subscribers to the newsletter contacted by Reuters denied having received such a report.
The talk, which hit currency markets late in the day, triggered previously set orders to sell dollars for yen and nearly wiped out early dollar gains vs. the mark.
"That must have been what caused the precipitous drop," said Cynthia Cooley, a foreign exchange analyst and trader at United Gulf Bank of Bahrain in Boston.
"The dollar was going down anyway. So when this story came out, that only exacerbated the situation," added Stephen Jury, chief dealer at Union Bank of Switzerland.
The dollar sank briefly to 116.95 yen, a level not seen since mid-January.
In late New York trading, the dollar settled at 117.23 yen, down from 118.67 yen late Tuesday. The dollar fetched 1.6947 German marks, up slightly from 1.6940 marks.

A surprising drop in a key gauge of inflation reported on Wednesday also weighed on the dollar as the data cast further doubt on prospects for a Federal Reserve interest rate hike next week. Higher rates would make yields on U.S. investments The Labour Department reported the Producer Price Index fell 0.6 percent in April, the largest decline since August 1993. With volatile food and energy items excluded, the index slid 0.1 percent.
Wall Street economists had expected the overall index to be unchanged in April, with the core up 0.1 percent.
Fed policymakers will meet next Tuesday to decide whether to tighten credit again. On March 25, they increased the federal funds target rate to 5.50 percent from 5.25 percent.

The Producer Price Index "added to the bearishness because as long as the perception is that the Fed is not tightening -- and I don't think it's priced in the market right now -- then you're going to see pressure on the dollar," said Edith Wolf, head of corporate sales at Credit Commerciale de France in New York.
The dollar had climbed briefly to 1.7085 marks in European trading after German central bank officials expressed approval of the current exchange rate between the two currencies.

By the time Bundesbank Vice President Johann Wilhelm Gaddum said the central bank was not especially concerned about the dollar's exchange rate, the currency had already retreated slightly below 1.70 marks in New York. After market rumours emerged, the dollar gave back even more gains.

The British pound rose after the Office for National Statistics reported that unemployment in Britain fell in April by 59,400 to 1.65 million, the lowest level in nearly seven years. The pound strengthened to $1.6470 from $1.6332.
The dollar fell to 1.4364 Swiss francs from 1.4375 francs, but rose to Canadian $1.3901 from C$1.3858.
